_disclaimer: READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING ANY NUMBER IN THIS FILE.
PRICES are real. Every input_cost/output_cost below was read from the
vendor's own pricing page on the _last_verified date, and each model
carries the URL it came from in its _source field. They are still only
true as of that date: vendors change prices and retire models, and
Registry.from_json warns once this file is more than 60 days old.
CAPABILITY SCORES ARE ESTIMATES. They are one engineer's priors about
relative model strength, not measurements. No benchmark was run to
produce them and none is implied. They are here so the catalog loads and
routes out of the box — replace them with numbers from your own evals on
your own traffic before using this to make real routing decisions. The
router is only as good as this field, which is why the README says the
catalog is the product.
LATENCY CLASSES are also estimates, assigned by tier rather than measured.
CONTEXT WINDOWS came from OpenRouter's public model index on 2026-08-16,
not from the vendor pages — a different and weaker provenance than the
prices above, recorded here so the difference is visible. They replaced
conservative placeholders that understated several models by 5x. The
router does not read this field yet (ROADMAP item 2); when it does, the
old placeholders would have excluded models that can do the work.
_provider_wiring: The 'provider' field must match a Provider name in your ProviderPool:
Four providers is deliberate: cross-lab auditing needs somewhere to cross to.
_pricing_caveats: gemini-3.7-flash is at promotional pricing through 2026-12-31; the page
states it rises to $1.50 in / $7.50 out on 2027-01-01.
gemini-3.1-pro-preview is priced in tiers; the rate here is the <=200k
input tier. Above 200k it is $4.00 in / $18.00 out.
DeepSeek's page notes dynamic peak/off-peak pricing starting 2026-08-16 --
one day after this file was verified. Re-check before relying on it.
Claude 4.7 and later use a newer tokenizer that produces roughly 30% more
tokens for the same text, so per-token price alone understates their
relative cost. Switchboard bills on observed token counts, so real runs
reflect this; the est_*_tokens on a Task do not.
Kimi prices are cache-MISS input rates; kimi-k3 cached input is $0.30 vs $3.00 uncached, a 10x swing Switchboard does not model.
kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed is the same model as kimi-k2.7-code at exactly double the price for ~180-260 tok/s output. It is in the catalog because it makes the latency weight mean something real.
A vendor listing a model in /models does not mean the chat endpoint accepts it. Verify with live_check.py --probe, which makes one 1-token call per model.

An independent index (OpenRouter) disagrees with six of these prices as of 2026-08-16 -- three by exactly half, which looks like a tier difference rather than a price change, and DeepSeek by more, on the day its dynamic peak/off-peak pricing began. Run examples/catalog_crosscheck.py to see the current disagreements. Only the vendor's own page settles them.
